title: AMD Ryzen 7 5800X3D 10th Anniversary Edition CPU $580 Delivered @ JW Computers via Woolworths Everyday Market
body:
Deal: AMD Ryzen 7 5800X3D 10th Anniversary Edition CPU $580 Delivered @ JW Computers via Woolworths Everyday Market

[Elyxar] Nice write up! My mobo doesn't even have wifi so that's how old my AM4 daily system is. Loved that the frequent socket changes stopped.
[UncleRico] Likewise. Fenvi 6E wifi cards can be had for under $20 on AliExpress and are a great after-market PCIE card, particularly those with seperate mountable antennas..
[Elyxar] I actually prefer wired for most of my gear. Not having wifi on that mobo was actually a choice.
[UncleRico] Always - wired > wireless every day of the week. Up until your network switch goes down or you drag your PC to some new location.
[Elyxar] @Rivet: That's really unfortunate. In the before times that wouldn't cost much but now… Are your switch/router and PC both surge protected?
[UncleRico] @Rivet: That's a lot of components to indivdually perish in a relatively short-time.
Even a basic UPS like this www.woolworths.com.au/shop/productdetails/1113676031/ion-f10… for under ~$80 may be benefitial if you have dirty incoming power. Either that or a 550w Corsair CX PSU for $59 from Amazon if it you have an unregulated non-Bronze PSU in your rig.
[S Baldrick] @Rivet: Depending on the value of your other components, it might still be worth getting a higher quality PSU from this tier list, and keeping your current one as a spare.
I think my old Seasonic was behind my Vega 64's stability issues, so I didn't take any chances and got an A tier Antec when I got a 9070 XT.
I'm thinking of getting some spare DDR4 RAM and putting the (overkill) fast kit from my NAS in storage, as a backup for the kit in my gaming PC. Don't want to take any chances with these shortages.
[Elyxar] @Rivet: Are you aware of how those surge protector boards work? They can only absorb so much before they no longer protect from surges. Some have a light that tells you if they still have surge protection capability or not (some the inverse). You can go from being protected to no protection in one zap. I also unplug when lightning is close (though now with some Bluettis I can unplug them and still continue watching offline media on TV).

[pedeyet762] There is also a 12700kf for $450 which would be $315 after cashback. Also works with cheaper ddr4. Not as fast as this in games but still faster than non-x3d ryzen 5000 cpus. Equivalent to 5900x in production workloads.
[axyh] Not if you can use the DDR4 RAM you already have on-hand.
I have a PC with 64GB of DDR4 that I bought for "future proofing" when RAM was cheap. You bet I'm upgrading the processor to ride out the next few years with the RAM I have.
Right now, anything that lets you use the hardware you already have for a little bit longer is a "bargain".

However, if you have DDR4 and also need a new motherboard, the i7-14700K is a better option IMO.
